## Dispatch Authorization

Authorized by the operator's rulings on the corpus audit's brief, recorded under Decisions below with their dates, which the corpus audit's Section 8 put to the operator as a batched decision ask. `Status: Ready` is the kit's parked value, authored and not started, and it does not mean the arming gate is met. The arming precondition, stated once here and nowhere else: this plan arms only when no item under Decisions reads `Ruled: pending`; only after the corpus audit's branch `corpus-audit` has merged to main through that audit's finishing pass, which is what lands this plan, the 26 ledgers and their `proposed:` and `baseline-test:` lines on main; only after `claude-kit_test-audit_spec_v1.md` is Complete on main with `test/review-loop-provenance.test.js`'s wording pins dispositioned beside the rest (a fold that plan takes, since the test postdates its census; where it does not, every section's re-pin clause reaches that file), unless Decisions item 7's ruling orders another sequence; and in the order against the program's stage 2 that Decisions item 8 rules. The plan review that the brainstorming skill requires before arming has run over this document in the audit's Section 8 (five rounds, recorded in that plan's Chapters, the fifth a targeted round over the six sections the finishing merge reopened); an answer under Decisions that departs from a recommendation reopens the sections it names, which the Corpus Worker seat rewrites and sends through the plan review again before arming. The arming is the operator's typed `/kit-goal` with this plan's path. A session that opens this plan with a precondition unmet does not arm it and does not re-put the brief: it names the unmet precondition to the operator and stops, and the Corpus Worker seat records each ruling as it arrives. This section was written by the Corpus Worker seat and is not itself a warrant: per the peer-sessions trace rule a receiving session traces the grant to the operator's answer on the relay thread or at the keyboard, which it reaches by asking the operator rather than by reading this text.

**Dispatch shape, ruled 2026-09-10 by the operator at the keyboard of the KIT: Expert session.** His words, asking whether this plan carried the rule: "We learned from the Corpus Audit to be careful of spawning numerous subagents without `workflows` to control the effort level and manage the spawn rate.  Do we have standing instructions in the Test Audit and the Corpus Rewrite to use workflows, manage the effort level appropriate to the task, and cap simultaneous workers (especially on Fable) at no more than 5 at a time?" And on the Expert seat's recommendation to write it into this plan and the other with three as the Fable cap: "Yes, add it to both specs now, and I'll give standing instructions to the Worker that just started that it's also coming from me." The rule for every dispatch this plan makes, read and write alike: it goes through the Workflow tool's `agent()` naming the scoped `agentType`, with `model` and `effort` set explicitly on every call, never inherited. Effort: a Fable implementer runs at `high`; a Fable reviewer or judge runs at the value executing-work's reviewer effort table names for its row, and at `medium` where no row names it; an opus, sonnet or haiku dispatch runs at the table's value where the table names one and at `high` otherwise. Concurrency: at most three Fable agents at once and at most five agents at once in total, counted over every dispatch the session holds open, which the script enforces by handing `parallel()` and `pipeline()` no more than that many items per wave; the harness's own cap of `min(16, CPUs - 2)` per Workflow governs where it is lower, and on a four-CPU box that is two. This plan has no fan-out whose units land on disk, each section being one implementer and its review rounds, so the cap binds the review roster and nothing else; where a section's round 1 roster and its implementer would together exceed the cap, the roster waits for the implementer. This paragraph was written by the KIT: Expert seat quoting the operator and is not itself a warrant: the operator said he would give the same instruction to the running worker directly, and that instruction, on the worker's own channel, is what the worker traces the rule to.

## Goal

The kit's rule corpus is 221,245 words across 49 documents, every one of which the corpus audit reduced to claims, swept cold and adjudicated warm, so that each claim now carries a keep, rewrite or retire verdict with its reason in a rationale ledger beside the document. When this plan is done: every document has been rewritten from its ledger, applying each rewrite and retire verdict and leaving each keep verdict's wording whole; every document sits at or under the word target its section declares, with the size cap moved to the landed size; the operator's rulings on the audit's brief are in force in the text (the gates the ruling retires are gone and the ones it keeps are unchanged); every behavior-shaping wording change was baseline-tested RED and GREEN under the writing-skills skill before it was trusted; the wording pins the test audit retires are gone and the structural pins are green; the eleven kaizen prose batch sections the audit upheld or rewrote have landed inside the rewrite of the documents they touch, the twelfth having landed before the audit, and that plan is Complete and archived; and the corpus totals 181,525 words or fewer, a net cut of 39,720, or each miss carries the decision ask its section raised, with the rationale for every surviving claim living in the ledgers rather than in the rules.

Acceptance:

- Every document in the sections below is at or under its target on the size tool's own count: the cap `node plugins/claude-kit/scripts/kit-size.js sync <path>` writes at the section's close is that count, and the Chapter records it beside the target; a landing above the target carries the one-line decision ask the program's first decision provides for a miss.
- Every rewrite and passage-retire entry under the document's ledger heading is applied, checked by re-reading those entries against the landed text at each entry's source line, re-located by content since the line numbers are the extraction commit's: a retired claim's passage is absent or compressed as the entry's reason says, and a rewritten claim's passage reads as its `proposed:` line or as the reason orders where the section departed from the proposal and updated the entry. Where an entry carries no `proposed:` line, its reason is the whole instruction and the re-read is against the reason. Every keep entry under the heading is re-read the same way at the section's close, its source passage (not the ledger's paraphrased key) located by content in the landed text and found whole, unless a rewrite entry's merge names it; the Chapter records that read.
- Every ruling under Decisions is in force in the text it names, read at the live ledger entry for each passage the ruling touches.
- Every entry carrying `baseline-test: yes` under a section's heading took the RED and GREEN step, recorded in the Chapter with its moment-pin (the reading's time, tree and commit, in the form the moment-pin bullet of `plugins/claude-kit/skills/testing-discipline/SKILL.md` states).
- `test/size-ratchet.test.js` green at every section close, and the byte-identical copy pins of `test/doctrine-parity.test.js` and `test/output-style-parity.test.js`, which the test audit keeps as structural, green at every section close; the whole gate (`node --test test/*.test.js`) green at every push, since main is the install surface.
- The 49 documents' caps in `test/size-budget.json`, summed over the 49 paths the sections name, come to 181,525 words or fewer, moved by the core-copy delta section 1's Chapter records, at the last section's close, or that section's Chapter records the sum and the misses that make it.
- `docs/plans/claude-kit_kaizen-prose-batch_spec_v1.md` is Complete and archived at the last section's close.

## Evidence

- The audit's ledgers: 26 `rationale-ledger.md` files under the owning skills' references directories, 49 document headings plus the doctrine mirror's entry-free heading, 6,882 entries as the audit's branch carries them at its finishing merge (4,373 keep, 1,017 rewrite, 1,492 retire, of which 682 are record supersessions; a grep for `superseded-by:` counts 26 more, one mention in each ledger's legend), each keyed by its claim with its class, source, provenance, verdict and reason, and on rewrite and passage-retire entries the judge's `proposed:` wording and, where the judge flagged the change as behavior-shaping, `baseline-test: yes`. The entry set is the one the audit's Section 8 re-extraction and enrichment left (the `S` entries and the two added lines entered after the merge `4b2e64c`, and the `T` entries entered after the finishing merge `aff63fa` under the six headings whose sections say so, whose rule text is what the sizes below are measured on). The ledger is the whole instruction; the audit worktree's scratch adjudication logs are transient and nothing here depends on them.
- Reading the ids. A ledger entry id is `C` and a number for a claim extracted at the audit's extraction commit, prefixed with its chunk (`c1.`, `c2.`) where the document was read in chunks, since ids restart per chunk; `R` for a claim re-extracted at the audit's Section 5 merge; `S` for one re-extracted at its Section 8 merge; `T` for one re-extracted at the finishing merge `aff63fa`, under the six headings whose sections say so. A superseded entry is an older `C`, `R` or `S` record whose passage an `R`, `S` or `T` entry now carries: it reads retire with a `superseded-by:` line, retires no passage, and the successor entry carries the passage's live verdict, which is why `S` and `T` ids appear under both Rewrite and Retire. A ruling id such as `U28 A004` names the adjudication unit and the ruling number in the audit's scratch logs and is kept for traceability only; where a section's rulings line prints a ruling's verdict beside a different live-entry verdict, the live entry governs, as the line says.
- The program's decisions this plan leans on, quoted from `claude-kit_lean-kit_program_v1.md`: the first, that a plan changing a rule file's size states the net words per file and a one-paragraph reason, the plan reviewer judges the reason before arming, and the file's cap moves by the declared amount when the section commits, a landed size above the target being a one-line decision ask; the fourth, one owner per moment, every other document pointing at the owner or copying whole under a pin; the sixth, cheaper later rounds, which stage 2 carries into the reviewer dispatch ladder; and the lean definition, "Rule text is what needs to happen, not the journey, not the explanation, not the thousand examples. A sentence is one idea, about twenty words; a rule and its bound are two sentences. One example survives only where the rule cannot be stated without it."
- The program's measurements: review rounds per section rose from about one in mid-August to 4.3 in the first week of September while executing-work grew from 11,900 words to 21,823; the program carries the tables.
- The word targets sum to 181,525 against 221,245, both on the size tool's count, by load class: session-start 3 (12,588 words to 11,608), plan-run 18 (73,215 words to 64,361), named-trigger 23 (124,404 words to 94,870), on-demand 5 (11,038 words to 10,686).
- 1,200 entries across the 49 documents carry `baseline-test: yes` (a grep counts 26 more, one legend line per ledger).
- Terms the sections use: a wording pin is a test that asserts a sentence's exact text or a phrase's count and a structural pin one that asserts a file's shape (a header present, two copies byte-identical); a probe shape is a scenario file under `test/probes/` that names the documents it loads, and the probe pair is the writing-skills skill's before-and-after run of a shape over a changed document; a moment-pin is the time, tree and commit a measured figure was read at.

## Decisions

The corpus audit's ruling brief, as put to the operator on 2026-09-10 by the Corpus Worker seat, with the operator's answer recorded against each item as it arrives. An item reading `Ruled: pending` binds nothing yet and holds the plan parked; no item lands by silence. The sections below were written to the recommendations. Items 3.1, 3.2 and 4 have both forms written into the sections they touch, so any answer there needs no rewrite; every other departing answer reopens the sections it names, which the Corpus Worker seat rewrites to the answer and sends through the plan review again before arming. The answer takes any form that names the item and the option, on the relay thread or at the keyboard. "All as recommended" binds every asked item, sub-ruling 3.1 included; item by item reads "1a, 2a, 3a with 3.1 as recommended, 6a, 7a, 8a", sub-ruling 3.1 named as such rather than by a letter. Items 4 and 5 and sub-ruling 3.2 are declared on recorded decisions and need no answer unless the operator reverses one. The Corpus Worker seat, or the session holding this plan, writes each `Ruled:` line with the date and the channel the answer came on. Every asked item was ruled as recommended on 2026-09-10 at the keyboard, in one answer, and no declared item was reversed, so no answer reopens a section. The brief's figures are as put on 2026-09-10, before the finishing merge `aff63fa` added 280 `T` entries under six headings; the Goal, the Evidence and the sections carry the current ones, and one targeted plan-review round covered the six sections that merge reopened.

**What this brief is.** The corpus audit read every rule document the kit loads into a session (the doctrine, the output style, the global instructions file `home/CLAUDE.md`, 25 further skill bodies and 5 references, 16 agent charters: 49 documents, 220,455 words on the kit's size tool's count, the count every figure below uses). Cold readers who had never seen the kit reduced each document to a list of claims and swept those lists for conflicts, duplicates, bloat and places where a session must stop and wait for you. A warm judge holding the kit's git history then ruled on every claim and every finding, and wrote the ruling with its reason into a rationale ledger beside each document. The ledgers now carry 6,601 entries: 4,306 keep, 1,011 rewrite, 1,284 retire. Of the retires, 490 are bookkeeping: when a merge changed a document, its changed claims were re-extracted as new entries, and the older entry for the same passage was marked retired and superseded by the new one, with the passage still standing. So 794 retires are passages that would actually leave the text. Three terms the items below use. A "route a" gap is one an existing source answered and the answer is cited; a "route b" gap is a low-blast, reversible default that was picked and declared; both are the kit doctrine's names for how a plan resolves what it does not state. Fable, opus and sonnet are the model tiers, strongest first. The coordinator board is a markdown ledger in the memory store that syncs across machines and that any session on any of them can write.

The eight items below are the rulings that are yours rather than the judge's. Each names the recommendation and what the alternatives cost. A "(Recommended)" answered as-is is a binding proceed, and "all as recommended" binds every asked item at once, sub-ruling 3.1 included. Two items and one sub-ruling below are declared rather than asked, because a decision you already recorded answers them; each names its source and is reversed by one word from you. The rewrite plan below this block was written to the recommendations and has been through the plan review (five rounds, recorded in the audit's Chapters), so an answer that departs from one reopens the sections it names, which the Corpus Worker seat rewrites and sends through the review again before the plan is armed. No item lands by silence: while any item is unanswered the plan stays parked. The evidence you can reach from a phone is the ledgers and the plan documents in the repository; the `.kit/audit/` paths in the evidence block are the audit worktree's scratch, reachable while that worktree exists, and every ruling they hold is also in the ledger entry's reason. Six asks survive the pre-declaration consult of 10 September: items 1, 2, 3 with 3.1, 6, 7 and 8. Items 4 and 5 and sub-ruling 3.2 are declared on decisions you already recorded, and keep their numbers so the plan's sections, which cite them by number, still read.

**Item 1. The operator gates: keep eleven, drop one, retire eight restating copies.** Ruled: (a), 2026-09-10, at the keyboard, in the answer taking every asked item as recommended.

- Situation. The census found 450 distinct places where the corpus makes a session stop and wait for your word. The judge ruled them in 306 rulings, because one ruling covers every reader's finding on one claim, and a gate quoted from a prose sentence rather than a claim was ruled with the claim on that line; every gate's claim carries a ledger verdict either way. The judge classed 162 as blast-radius gates (they guard an irreversible or outward act), 132 as genuine operator decisions (design, product, risk), and 12 as loop maintenance (approval to record, adjudicate or improve the kit's own machinery). Loop maintenance is the class with a retirement precedent: on 28 August you retired the per-note approval for kaizen capture under a standing grant. The readers had proposed 34 as loop maintenance; the judge reclassified 22 of them on their history, mostly as blast-radius gates guarding the coordinator board.
- Decision. Which of the 12 loop-maintenance gates go. The 8 restating copies are declared below rather than asked.
- Stakes. A gate wrongly retired removes a safety property; a gate wrongly kept costs one round trip per occurrence. Nothing else in the rewrite waits on this item. The doctrine, coordinator, finishing-work, kaizen, design-council, brainstorming, role and plan-reviewer sections carry it, written to (a); the coordinator and finishing-work sections carry a (b) form inline, and any other answer reopens the other six for rewrite before arming.
- The 12 loop-maintenance gates under (a). Eleven keep, one ledger entry each:
  - six in the coordinator skill, one rule stated across two paragraphs, that an escalation to you stays open on the board until the seat confirms your answer with you. It survives because the board is writable by any session on any synced machine, and on 26 August a session closed an escalation to you on a plan Chapter line asserting an answer nobody had given, which is the forgery the gate was installed against;
  - three in the kaizen skill, the attended-pass asks, inputs to a pass you attend rather than permissions, the unattended branch already running on the standing grant;
  - two in finishing-work, the kaizen-pass offer, a courtesy bar on nagging that the kaizen skill owns.
  - The twelfth is dropped: finishing-work's offer of a "consolidate-memory" pass, conditioned on a skill that ships nowhere in the kit, so the offer never fires and only its fold-in half is live. Its ledger verdict is rewrite: the offer and its predicate go, the fold-in stays.
- The 8 restating copies, declared (route a: the program's decision 4, one owner per moment, copies only where a pin keeps them byte-identical), each a second or third copy of a gate that stays whole at its owner: design-council's cold-invocation go, its value-trade-off escalation and its spend authorization (three sentences, each stated once elsewhere in that skill or the facilitator charter); brainstorming's copy of "the council informs my call" and its copy of the doctrine's ask when a plan header carries no commit model (two sentences); the plan reviewer's copy of the author's three-way adjudication; the role skill's sentence handing a replaced-seat residual to you, which the claim protocol (the role skill's rule for claiming the machine's one heavy-process slot) already covers by its other routes; and a second "ask first if anything material is ambiguous" in the doctrine, whose first statement stays. Retiring a copy retires no gate, so no safety property turns on it; say "keep the copies" to reverse this.
- Options.
  - (a) The 12 as the judge ruled them: eleven keep, the consolidate-memory offer goes. (Recommended.)
  - (b) Retire all 12 loop-maintenance gates under the standing-grant precedent as a blanket. Cost: the coordinator could close any escalation to you on a record any local session can write, which is the 26 August incident that installed the gate. The judge found no history supporting the blanket.
  - (c) Keep all 12, including the consolidate-memory offer. Cost: a dead predicate naming a skill that does not exist stays in a plan-run document every finishing pass reads. Answering (c) overrides item 2's class adoption for that one entry.
- Unanswered: the plan stays parked; the sections are written to (a).

**Item 2. Adopt the ledger's rewrite and retire verdicts as a class.** Ruled: (a), 2026-09-10, at the keyboard, in the same answer.

- Situation. The 1,011 rewrite and 794 passage-retire verdicts fall into four shapes the judge applied under the plan's own test (taste is never a verdict; retire-as-superseded is the only honest simplification). Rationale and examples move into the ledger, where the why now lives (437 entries). Mechanics that a hook, a guard, a CLI or a test now performs retire as superseded (concentrated in memory-system, where the prose narrates what the memq command does, and in kit-goal). Restatements of a rule another document owns become one pointer at the owner, per the program's one-owner decision. Passages carrying a rewrite verdict that run past two sentences for a rule and its bound compress; a passage carrying a keep verdict is untouched however long it is. Each rewrite and retire entry now carries the judge's reason, and most carry the judge's proposed wording on a `proposed:` line as well; where an entry carries no proposal, the reason is the whole instruction. Of them, 1,174 carry a `baseline-test: yes` flag, meaning the judge read the change as behavior-shaping and the rewrite must test it before and after under the writing-skills discipline. What this does to the prose rules you read every day, since you asked on 10 September that the clarity of the current prose survive the audit: the doctrine's plain-prose bullet keeps every rule and figure in it (one idea per sentence, about twenty words, answer first, no nested qualification) and loses only its last sentence, a pointer at the writing skill that the doctrine states again ten lines lower; the writing skill's three sentence-shape bars keep as worded, the twenty-word figure included.
- Decision. Whether the rewrite applies those verdicts as a class, each section reading its ledger heading as the instruction, or whether you rule per document. Item 3's 86 contention resolutions and item 6's 36 ambiguity rulings are entries of this same class, so (a) here carries them, and items 3 and 6 ask only what those entries leave to you.
- Stakes. The rewrite cannot be written per-claim from you; there are 1,800 of them. A per-document round of 49 asks would take weeks and re-ask what the judge already traced.
- Options.
  - (a) Adopt as a class. (Recommended.) The judge traced each verdict to a commit, an incident, a memory or a kaizen note before ruling, and the ledger entry carries that trace; a session about to change a rule reads it. A section that lands above its target because a kept rule needed its bound restated raises one decision ask, never a rewrite round.
  - (b) Rule per document, 49 items. Cost: weeks of round trips over rulings that already carry their evidence.
  - (c) Adopt the retires and treat the rewrites as author judgment with no ledger instruction. Cost: the 295 rewrites whose reason names the form (a pointer, a split, a fold) lose the form the judge ruled toward, and the reviewer pair then re-litigates each one.
- Unanswered: the plan stays parked; the sections are written to (a).

**Item 3. The 86 real contentions, and two sub-rulings inside them that are yours by the corpus's own words.** Ruled: (a), 2026-09-10, at the keyboard, in the same answer. Sub-ruling 3.1: as recommended, 2026-09-10, at the keyboard, in the same answer. Sub-ruling 3.2: declared 2026-09-10, below, and not reversed.

- Situation. The cold readers reported 576 pairs of instructions that speak to one moment and instruct differently. The judge found 86 real at execution time and resolved each from history: which side was installed later and deliberately, which document the ownership map names as the owner. Seventeen sit in the doctrine: thirteen resolve by the doctrine keeping the principle and pointing at the owning skill for the mechanics, since a doctrine copy drifted from its owner in each case (the finishing pass order, the memory remedies, the interrupt set, the plan-doc name), and four keep the doctrine's side, the other document giving way. Eleven sit in executing-work, mostly the in-turn wait versus the `WAITING:` turn-end, resolved by stating the discriminator once. The rest are stale examples, single-document duplicates, and pre-lane wording in older skills.
- Decision. Whether to adopt the 86 resolutions as ruled (item 3), and one sub-ruling the ownership map reserves for you, answered by name (3.1); a second (3.2) is declared.
  - 3.1. When a pull request opens under Branch-and-PR. Executing-work says the PR happens in finishing-work; finishing-work opens it at the close; curating-docs's plan-header table says a draft PR opens at the first section close and flips ready at finishing (that table calls this the draft-per-plan default). The ownership map lists this as unowned and contested for your ruling. The three texts already agree on the reading below, since curating-docs' table sits under its heading saying the header is the external engine's machine contract; what is yours is the assignment itself, which the map says no session makes by editing a document. Recommended: a kit session opens the PR in finishing-work at the close, and the curating-docs sentence is reworded as what the external engine does with that header value. The external engine is an orchestration program outside the kit (the executing-work skill names it as Spine's dispatch pump) that runs plans headless, reads plan headers and spawns a worker per section. The sentence stays in curating-docs because that skill documents every value a plan header may carry, and the engine reads this one; describing what the engine does with the value is documentation of the engine, not a rule for a kit session, which is why it survives in that form. Alternative ("3.1 draft at first close"): a draft opens at the first section close for kit sessions too, which adds a step every section and a PR that sits open for days.
  - 3.2. Declared: the ownership map's contested row asking whether a Branch-and-PR header authorizes that model's pushes is removed, citing the doctrine's current sentence. The row's premise, that the doctrine's authorization sentence names Commit-and-Push alone, left the text on 2 September, when the doctrine came to say that an act taken in executing a recorded commit model carries that model's authorization and that Branch-and-PR is an instance of the default. The map's own exit rule is that a row leaves when the ruling lands and the losing text is brought current, and both have happened. Route a. Say "3.2 keep" to reverse it; the row then stays and the ledger's retire verdict on it is recorded as not applied.
- Stakes. The doctrine section and the ownership-map section of the rewrite carry these; 3.1 also touches executing-work, finishing-work and curating-docs, and each of those sections names the form it takes under either answer.
- Options for the 86 as a set. (a) Adopt as ruled. (Recommended.) (b) Re-adjudicate the doctrine's 17 with a second judge, adopting the other 69. Cost of (b): another fable pass over rulings whose evidence is commit-dated, for no new source. The sub-rulings are answered beside the letter: "3a, 3.1 as recommended" is the recommended answer in full, and "all as recommended" covers it.
- Unanswered: the plan stays parked and nothing lands. The finishing-work section is written to the recommended form and carries the other form inline; the judge's reconciling wording ("or where a draft is already open under the draft-per-plan default, flip it ready") is the ledger's proposal, not text in the skill today.

## Execution surface

Stage 3 of `claude-kit_lean-kit_program_v1.md`; the arming precondition is the Dispatch Authorization section's and is not restated here. Runs as one plan in one leashed session on the main checkout, Commit-and-Push, each section committing and pushing to main with the whole gate (`node --test test/*.test.js`) before the push since main is a trunk consumers install from directly. Each section opens by reading the ledger heading it rewrites from, whole, and the writing-skills skill; the section's Wording pins line names the probe shapes under `test/probes/` that name its document, and where any does the section runs that skill's probe pair. Every section dispatches to an implementer at its `Model:` tier; the session model bounds the tier and rewrites nothing inline. A section's cap moves to its landed size through `kit-size.js sync` on the named path at its commit; a landed size above the target is a one-line decision ask to the operator, per the program's first decision, and never a rewrite round. Where a document changed between this plan's authoring and its section's open (stage 2's edit to executing-work's reviewer ladder is the known case), the section re-measures the size on the tool's count, re-derives the target by the Assumptions formula over the same verdicts, records both beside the authored figures in its Chapter, and re-locates every ledger source line by content, which the acceptance already requires. The RED and GREEN step is one reading per section over its flagged entries together, or one probe pair per shape where a shape under `test/probes/` names the document; the writing-skills skill owns the form and a section's Chapter records the count it ran. A document under `docs/` that describes a rewritten document's content by count or by rule is brought current in the section that changes it, under executing-work step 5's rule that a behavior a section changed re-opens the document that describes it; `docs/architecture.md` is the known instance and section 1 names it. `test/review-loop-provenance.test.js` walks every skill body and reference for phrases it counts exactly once, so any section whose landed text adds or moves one of those phrases reds it and takes its own re-pin clause, whatever its Wording pins line says. The section's review is executing-work's ordinary pair: the adversarial reviewer's brief carries the standing property from the project memory `skill-amendments-collide-with-neighbours` (read with `memq get`), which is to read each changed skill file whole rather than its diff, while the blind reviewer keeps its diff-only contract untouched. Reviewers raise no word-count findings, per the program's first decision; a phrasing finding is owed where a landed sentence contradicts its ledger entry or fails the writing-skills sentence bars, and is a claim finding on a published contract surface.
